assumptions: The current baseline and exact fixture bytes are authoritative for this analysis.
Input positions are meaningful; equal urgency preserves their relative order and ticket IDs do not resolve ties.
The scenario validity constraints are later coding requirements, not a current decision about invalid-input behavior.
A separate result list preserves input sequence and values during ordering; deep copying records is not a stated requirement.

differences.complementary: Construction, invariant reasoning and boundary/example reasoning support one positional ordering rule; the proposal combines those distinct contributions without voting or concatenating drafts.
differences.evidence: A and C report executable boundary checks, while B distinguishes its fixture execution from boundary reasoning. The senior independently checked six in-memory examples and all registered source digests; no candidate test claim is treated as a production implementation result.
differences.exclusive: Batch error and partial results with a rejection report are incompatible eventual interface commitments if imposed together. All three candidates explicitly keep them as alternatives; deferral satisfies the current criterion, so no conflict blocks this analysis. A later authorized coding baseline must select and define the interface.
differences.scope: All candidates analyze the whole valid-input ordering problem and compare both invalid-input policies. Later coding constraints supply validity context but do not authorize implementation or select policy for the current analysis.
differences.terminology: Candidate B labels output positions from zero, while A and C use one-based output positions and C presents one-based input positions. The synthesis labels one-based output and zero-based input positions; all refer to the identical t1,t3,t2,t4 sequence.

interfaces: Valid records yield every input position exactly once in descending urgency and stable tie order, with no input mutation.
For a later batch-error policy, define the exception and diagnostic contract before implementation.
For a later rejection-report policy, define the result/report shape, duplicate-ID treatment and complete per-position acceptance or rejection accounting before implementation.
No implementation, exception selection, rejection-report shape or user preference is adopted by this analysis synthesis.
omitted: Duplicate descriptions of the same ordering rule, fixture tables and policy comparisons are consolidated into one coherent account; every candidate remains represented.
Candidate-local completion statements and sibling-read claims are not adopted as manager acceptance or independent senior evidence.
No source alternative is silently discarded. Future exception selection and rejection-report shape remain unchosen because the current analysis baseline explicitly defers them.
requirements: ordering-analysis: Descending urgency and stable equal-urgency input order are specified by the opening rule, construction and invariants.
ordering-analysis: The complete exact-fixture output is t1,t3,t2,t4 and includes all four original records once.
valid-input-policy: Error and explicit rejection-report policies are compared and remain explicitly deferred without inferred user preference.
retained: analysis_a_v1 retains the negative-urgency/original-position construction, complete record result, new-list preservation boundary and comparison-sort complexity analysis.
analysis_b_v1 retains conservation, descending urgency, stability and preservation invariants; unique positional ordering; reversal risk; complete accepted/rejected position accounting.

analysis_c_v1 retains the full-fixture and endpoint explanation, empty/singleton/all-equal/already-ordered consequences, ID tie-break counterexample and current-versus-future policy authority boundary.
risks: An implementation that reverses an ascending result or uses IDs for tie breaking can violate stability.
Silent filtering, coercion or undefined duplicate-ID accounting can violate the selected later validation interface.
A later change to fixture, baseline, dependencies or candidate bytes requires current-version reassessment.
This analysis does not prove an implementation or invalid-input runtime behavior; those require later authorized work.
